def transform(grid):
    # Separator rows and columns split the image into rectangular panels.
    # Mark a panel when it contains exactly two foreground cells.
    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    sep = grid[0][0]  # overwritten below; separators are the most common lines
    # Find uniform separator rows/columns, excluding the panel background.
    row_seps = [r for r, row in enumerate(grid) if len(set(row)) == 1 and len(set(grid[r])) == 1]
    # A separator row is uniform and differs from the ordinary cell background.
    # The background is the most frequent value among non-separator cells.
    from collections import Counter
    vals = Counter(v for row in grid for v in row)
    sep_color = max(set(v for row in grid for v in row), key=lambda v: sum(x == v for row in grid for x in row))
    # Main background is typically the second-most common color; infer from nonuniform rows.
    nonsep_vals = Counter(v for r,row in enumerate(grid) if r not in row_seps for v in row)
    bg = nonsep_vals.most_common(1)[0][0]
    row_seps = [r for r in row_seps if grid[r][0] != bg]
    col_seps = [c for c in range(w) if len({grid[r][c] for r in range(h)}) == 1 and grid[0][c] != bg]
    def ranges(n, seps):
        out=[]; start=0
        for s in seps:
            if start < s: out.append((start,s))
            start=s+1
        if start<n: out.append((start,n))
        return out
    rr, cc = ranges(h,row_seps), ranges(w,col_seps)
    foreground = max((v for v in vals if v != bg and v not in {grid[0][c] for c in col_seps}), key=lambda v: vals[v])
    return [[1 if sum(grid[r][c] == foreground for r in range(r0,r1) for c in range(c0,c1)) == 2 else bg for c0,c1 in cc] for r0,r1 in rr]
